**What this PR does / why we need it**:
Preconditions should retry internally on stale watch data instead of surfacing an error.

leaving in the milestone for visibility as we root cause whether this is a test-only issue or not

I spent a while trying to recreate this and could not (again). I made one of the tests hotloop with QPS 100 doing get/update of the status subresource, then ran that in parallel with the other integration tests in the package. No failures found after running for ~10 minutes.

Updated description with testgrid link to locate recent flakes (https://k8s-testgrid.appspot.com/google-unit#integration-master&include-filter-by-regex=apiextensions-apiserver%2Ftest%2Fintegration&width=5&sort-by-flakiness=), found a couple in the last week.

iiuc, the error comes from apiserver [comparing](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/18559013ec0e8d3f4290b4c83386a404e148ec3b/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/store.go#L276-L278) the [requested obj](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/18559013ec0e8d3f4290b4c83386a404e148ec3b/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/update.go#L174) UID against the [watch cache](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/18559013ec0e8d3f4290b4c83386a404e148ec3b/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cacher.go#L738-L741). The requested obj is up-to-date since it was from etcd, but I didn't see mechanism that guarantees the watch cache to be up-to-date after a "delete-create" or "delete-create-get" sequence (the cacher implementation for Delete, Create and Get(rv="") go through etcd directly). Is this failure an expected behavior, and should we just retry on precondition failure?

the triage page seems to be stale, filed https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/issues/14186
